content:
The decay is \(\pi^+ \to \mu^+ + \nu_\mu\) with the pion at rest.  
Given rest masses: \(m_\pi = 139.6\text{ MeV}\), \(m_\mu = 105.7\text{ MeV}\), \(m_\nu = 0\).

By conservation of energy and momentum, the momentum magnitude \(p\) of both products satisfies:
\[
m_\pi = \sqrt{p^2 + m_\mu^2} + p
\]
Solving for \(p\):
\[
p = \frac{m_\pi^2 - m_\mu^2}{2m_\pi} = \frac{(139.6)^2 - (105.7)^2}{2 \times 139.6} \text{ MeV}
\]
The kinetic energy of the neutrino is simply \(KE_\nu = p\).  
The kinetic energy of the muon is \(KE_\mu = \sqrt{p^2 + m_\mu^2} - m_\mu = \frac{(m_\pi - m_\mu)^2}{2m_\pi}\).

Numerically:
\[
m_\pi - m_\mu = 33.9 \text{ MeV}
\]
\[
KE_\mu = \frac{(33.9)^2}{2 \times 139.6} = \frac{1149.21}{279.2} \approx 4.12 \text{ MeV}
\]
\[
KE_\nu = \frac{(33.9)(139.6 + 105.7)}{279.2} = \frac{33.9 \times 245.3}{279.2} \approx 29.8 \text{ MeV}
\]

These match option (A).

Answer: A
